summary:
## Overview
This guide covers how to play "Two Ghosts" by Harry Styles on an acoustic guitar. The lesson uses a guitar in **standard tuning**, and **no capo** is required.

## Strumming Pattern
The majority of the song uses one consistent strumming pattern:
*   **`Down Down-Up Up-Down-Up Down-Up`**

> [!NOTE]
> In the chorus, the **A to E** chord change happens within one pattern. Play `Down Down-Up` on the **A chord**, then switch to **E** for the remaining `Up-Down-Up Down-Up`.

## Chord Voicings & Progressions

### Intro & Verse
*   **Progression**: E → F#m → G#m → F#m

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The **F# minor (F#m)** and **G# minor (G#m)** chords use a specific voicing, not standard barre chords.
> *   **F#m**: Ring/Pinky on 4th fret (A & D strings), Index on 2nd fret (G string). Strum from the 5th (A) string down, leaving the top two strings open.
> *   **G#m**: Use the exact same hand shape as F#m, but move it up two frets. Strum from the 5th string down.

### Chorus
*   **Line 1 (played twice)**: A → E (using the split strumming pattern)
*   **Line 2**: C#m → B → A → G#m (all single down-strums) → F#m (one full strumming pattern)
*   **Line 3**: C#m → B → A (single down-strums, hold the A)
*   **Chorus 2 & 3**: The first and second lines are each played twice before moving to the third line.

> [!TIP]
> If you struggle with barre chords, you can substitute the **B chord** with a simpler **B power chord**.

### Bridge
*   **Progression**: E → G#m → Bm → F#m
*   Each chord is played for one full strumming pattern.

## Lead Guitar Parts

### Intro / Break Riff
This melodic riff is played over the verse progression and uses slides, pull-offs, and a bend.
*   It starts on the 5th fret of the 2nd (B) string.
*   Features a quick slide from the 4th to the 7th fret on the 1st (E) string.
*   Includes a slide up from the 7th to 9th fret and back down on the 1st string.
*   The riff ends with a pull-off from the 5th to the 4th fret (1st string), followed by a bend and release on the 5th fret of the 2nd string.

> [!NOTE]
> The **Outro riff** is a simplified version of the intro riff that omits the final pull-off and bend section.

### Solo
 The solo is played entirely with finger slides to emulate a slide guitar.
*   It is primarily played on the **2nd (B) string**, sliding between the **5th, 7th, and 9th frets**.
*   The phrase ends with a slide on the **3rd (G) string** from the **4th to the 6th fret**.

## Performance: "Two Ghosts"

Same lips red, same eyes blue, same white shirt, couple more tattoos. But it's not you and it's not me. Tastes so sweet, looks so real. Sounds like something that I used to feel, but I can't touch what I see. We're not who we used to be. We're not who we used to be. We're just two ghosts standing in the place of you and me.

## Lesson Introduction

Good day guys, my name's Dave and welcome to another Guitar Zero to Hero song tutorial. And by request today, I'll be teaching you how to play Two Ghosts by Harry Styles. So for the basics, you'll need your guitar in standard tuning and you won't need a capo. Now, if you want to master your chords back to front, then be sure to head over to guitarzerohero.com to pick up my free guitar ebook. All right, so let's get stuck into the intro/verse.

## Verse Chord Voicings

And it's a really easy four-chord chord progression. We start with an E major chord. Our second chord, for the sake of this lesson, we're just going to call an F sharp minor, but it's actually going to be a little bit different to your typical F sharp minor barre chord. We're going to play it the way that Harry Styles plays it in his live video. So you're going to take your ring and pinky finger and put them on the fourth fret of the fifth and fourth strings, and your index finger will go on the second fret of the third string. You'll leave the first and second strings open, and you'll just be strumming from the fifth string onwards. And that's what we're going to call our F sharp minor chord for this song.

Now, if you want to be a little more fancy, what you can do is actually play the bass note of this F sharp minor by taking your thumb and reaching over and hitting the second fret of the sixth string. Now that might challenge the beginners out there, so you can just mute that sixth string and play from the fifth string onwards. And that's actually what Harry Styles does.

Third chord shape is exactly the same, but just moved up two frets. So that whole shape just remains exactly the same. You just go one, two, and everything else is exactly the same. Again, if you want to play that bass note, you just reach your thumb over and push down on the fourth fret of the sixth string. But again, Harry Styles just plays from the fifth string onwards and he mutes that sixth string. We're going to call this chord our G sharp minor. And then for our fourth chord in this chord progression, we go back to our F sharp minor.

## Main Strumming Pattern

Now for the strumming pattern, we have one strumming pattern that we'll use throughout the whole song, which will be really nice and easy. The strumming pattern will go something like this: down, down-up, up, down-up, down-up. And in succession: down, down-up, up, down-up, down-up. Down, down-up, up, down-up, down-up. You're going to play that strumming pattern once for each chord in this intro/verse and it will sound like this. Down, down-up, up, down-up, down-up. Down, down-up, up, down-up, down.

## First Chorus: Structure & Chords

Now we get to our first chorus, and we have three lines of chords here. Our first line of chords goes A to an E chord. Now, these two chords are going to be within one strumming pattern. The point at which you're going to change from the A to the E is going to be on that first up strum. So it will sound like this: down, down, up, up, down, down. Now you're going to play that first line twice, and then we get to our second line of chords which is really nice and easy. So we have a row of four chords which aren't going to be played for a strumming pattern, they're just going to be all strummed once. So we start with the C sharp minor. So you have your index finger on the fourth fret of the fifth string, ring and pinky on the sixth fret of the fourth and third strings, and your middle finger will go on the fifth fret of the second string. Now you don't have to bar that fourth fret with your index finger; you can just be pushing down that fourth fret of the fifth string and leave your index finger up so that this first string is just open. So that's our C sharp minor. Then we go to our B barre chord. Now that's going to be a bit of a stretch for the beginners out there, so if you're having troubles playing that B chord, you can just play a B power chord, which is a lot easier. Then we go to an A chord, and then we go to our G sharp minor chord that we have in our intro. And then we're going to go to our F sharp minor chord shape and we're going to play it for one strumming pattern. So in total, our second line sounds like this. And then we get to our third line, which is just three chords. We have our C sharp minor, B chord, and then A, and you just hold on that A chord and that's it. So in total, our first chorus will sound like this. Down, down-up, up-down-up, down. Down, down-up, up-down-up, down.

## Chorus 2 & 3 Variations

Now for Chorus 2 and Chorus 3, we're going to be tweaking it a tiny bit. We're still going to have the same three lines, but the first and second lines are played through twice, and then you get to the third line. So for Chorus 2 and Chorus 3 it will sound like this. Down, down-up, up-down-up, down.

## Bridge Chord Progression

And the last section we need to learn is the bridge, and it's really easy. It's just a four-chord chord progression. We're going to start with our E chord, and then we're going to go to our G sharp minor chord shape. Then we're going to go to a B minor. Now we haven't used this anywhere else in the song. It's a B minor barre chord shape. Now if you're having troubles playing that B minor, you can just play the B power chord shape. And then you can add that middle finger and then the barre once you get more comfortable. And then our final chord for this chord progression is an F sharp minor chord shape. We're going to be playing each chord for one strumming pattern and the bridge will just sound like this.

## Intro, Break & Outro Lead Riff

Now I'm going to quickly teach you the lead parts in this song. We'll start with our intro and break lead riff, and it's really nice and easy. We start with the fifth fret of the second string with our middle finger, then with our index finger we'll go on the fourth fret of the first string, hit that and slide up to the seventh fret. So that's all in one quick motion. Fifth fret, fourth, slide up to the seventh, like that. We do it again. And then once we're up at the seventh fret, we're going to pluck the first string again, slide up to the ninth fret and slide back down to the seventh fret, but you're only going to pluck that once, so you slide up and down. Then we're going to play the fifth fret, fourth fret, and slide to the seventh again. And then for this last section, we're going to hit the fifth fret with our middle finger of the first string and pull off to the fourth fret. And then with your ring finger, you'll go to the fifth fret of the second string, and then you'll pluck it again and bend it up and then release it back down. So that last chunk all together, and the whole intro/break riff.

Now whilst we have this fresh in our head, for the outro, it's exactly the same except we're not playing this last chunk. Everything else is exactly the same for this outro lead riff.

## Guitar Solo Breakdown

So now I'm going to teach you the solo and it's really nice and easy. Now this is actually played with a slide in the recording but I know most of you probably won't have one, so I'll just teach you an easy way of playing it. So we're going to start by sliding up to the fifth fret of the second string with our index finger. Now you can slide up from any position if you want, just as long as it's quick so that you can't really tell where that slide came from. But if you want a starting point, you can just use the third fret and slide up from there. So after that fifth fret, we're going to slide up, we're going to pluck that and slide up to the seventh fret. And then for our next chunk, we're going to slide from the seventh fret to the ninth fret. Then we're going to go down to the seventh fret, pluck that; fifth fret, pluck that; pluck that fifth fret again and then slide up to the seventh fret. So far we have this.

Then we're going to slide from the seventh fret to the ninth fret again, go to the seventh fret, pluck that; go to the fifth fret, pluck that. And then we're going to go to our fourth fret of the third string, hit that and slide to the sixth fret. Then you're going to pluck that sixth fret again, and then we go to the fourth fret, slide up to the sixth, and then repeat that again. So that last chunk, and the first line in total.

Now the second line of this solo is exactly the same as that first line, except we just don't play that last chunk that goes like this. And that's the whole solo.

So now I'm going to be playing through this song in its entirety. I'm going to have a vocal track on top for some context so feel free to play this back as many times as you'd like to practice, play along to and see how you go.
